incomplete_fix_quote: The current "single-pass" regex approach is insufficient against nested sequences. By using nested traversal sequences (e.g., ....//), an attacker can bypass directory traversal protections (CWE-184: Incomplete List of Disallowed Inputs).
root_cause: server/api/command/index.js /api/download applied a SINGLE-PASS sanitizer `req.query.name.replace(new RegExp('../','g'), '')` (added by the CVE-2023-31718 fix). One pass removes the inner `../` of a nested `....//` and the leftover `..` + `/` re-forms a valid `../`, so the traversal survives. FUXA 1.2.11 replaces it with normalizeRelativePath()+resolveWithin() (server/api/path-helper.js) which reject any '..' segment and enforce base-dir containment.
sink_relationship: SAME sink for seed and residual (GET /api/download report-download). Variant A (same-sink encoding bypass). The 1.2.11 patch also fixes the identical single-pass regex on /api/logs, /api/upload, /api/resources/remove; /api/download was chosen because it is the exact endpoint of the CVE-2023-31718 seed.
impact_note: CVE-2026-25951 is documented primarily as arbitrary file WRITE -> RCE (via /api/upload into runtime/scripts). This case instruments the READ manifestation on the same single-pass-regex weakness at /api/download (the seed's own endpoint), which is a clean read-exfil canary and faithful to the shared root cause. Auth: FUXA default settings leave secureEnabled unset -> the admin endpoint is reachable without a token.
